headline: We ask your
forgiveness.
metaldock.reading: Prakrit for something harder than sorry. Not an excuse and not an explanation — a wish that the harm be made fruitless, as though it had never landed.
metaldock.caption:
We ask your forgiveness.

Micchami Dukkadam — Prakrit, and it does not mean sorry. miccha: fruitless, void. dukkada: a badly done deed. Not an excuse and not an explanation, but a wish that the harm be made fruitless, as though it had never landed.

Wherever we have caused harm this year, knowingly or unknowingly, in thought, word or deed — we ask your forgiveness.

Metal Dock · Stainless Steel Supply · www.metaldock.co.in

dockfinity.ask: A year of building leaves marks. A date we missed, a message sent sharper than it needed to be, a promise that slipped.
dockfinity.to: To our clients, our partners and our own team — we ask your forgiveness.
dockfinity.caption:

The phrase is Prakrit, and it is not an apology. miccha — fruitless, void. dukkada — a badly done deed. It asks that the harm be made fruitless, as though it had never landed.

A year of building leaves marks. A date we missed, a message sent sharper than it needed to be, a promise that slipped.

To our clients, our partners and our own team — we ask your forgiveness.
